races.name: Download The At The Races App Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: In The City
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who handles good ground well (three of last five on good, placed twice), trained by Greatrex whose yard is 0/5 in 14 days — a concerning in-form dip — but Rose Dawes can park this filly close to Moe's Legacy and that tracking position is the race's most coveted tactical slot over Windsor's flat 5f.

runners_data.name: Dark Alley
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Greatrex, whose 14-day strike rate of 0/5 warrants a flag; six races on good ground produce only one win on firmer, and dropping to 5f from six, the last run at 5f on good produced only a seventh — the closing style is a real concern when there is just one genuine pace-setter to chase.

runners_data.name: Too Darn Good
runners_data.note: A natural backmarker who has been moved into mid-division on the map because the hold-up cohort is simply too large to all sit at the rear; the honest read is that this horse wants to come from off the pace, but on a 5f Windsor flat track with a single, controlled front-runner, finishing from the back is extremely difficult — the redistribution meaningfully erodes its chance.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 55, and a hold-up type for Patrick Owens (0/3 in 14 days) whose form in similar going is a modest 2 from 6 runnings — like Too Darn Good, this filly's natural late-running style cannot be accommodated in its preferred position given the field composition, compounding the already slim claims on ratings.

runners_data.name: Moe's Legacy
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field and the race's pivotal horse — Jack Nicholls steers a 5yo carrying 142lbs with a visor, and 66 days off since the last run is worth noting; its style_fit tag reflects that Moe's Legacy tends to race prominently rather than lead from the front in the purest sense, but in this field it has the lead by default and that is a powerful tactical gift.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Christopher Mason (2/7 in 14 days, the field's joint-best active trainer strike rate) whose best form at 5f on good came with a win on soft and a poor run of ninth on fast ground; Ryan Kavanagh takes the ride and the recent form (5-1-14-9-9) reads as inconsistent even if that Windsor fifth on good is mildly encouraging.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up handler for Cook & Bridger (0/9 in 14 days) who returns just 14 days since last run — the trainer's current drought is a material concern; form at 5f on good ground spans 11 runs with zero wins and three places, suggesting this horse finds a way to be competitive without converting, and the hold-up style in a one-pace-setter race limits upside.

runners_data.name: Beaumadier
runners_data.note: Genuinely hold-up by inclination and among the redistributed horses most likely to find a true backmarker berth given strong 5f course-type form — three of its last five runs at exactly 5f on good ground produced a second and a third; Hope Regan takes a 7lb claim for Loughnane (1/11 in 14 days), and if any closer can thread through late, this six-year-old's consistency at this trip and surface gives it the best grounds to do so.

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: The other redistributed closer most credibly able to race from the back — five of the last five runs include two seconds, a third and a third on similar going, giving Stuart Williams's horse the strongest closing-form profile in the field; Chloe Lyons claims 7lbs, the trainer is 5/28 in 14 days (useful), and a tongue-tie and visor combination signals the yard is trying to extract the full effort, but the fundamental problem remains: a lone front-runner at 5f Windsor rarely suits genuine closers.

runners_data.name: London Is Blue
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with two wins on good ground already at 6f and a second on good at 5f — the form profile reads as a horse who wants further than 5f sprinting, but Robert Cowell (0/9 in 14 days) sends Jack Callan in, and the winning profile on good-to-firm in recent runs makes the going no barrier; the hold-up style is its natural mode and the class peak (OR 73 here, won at OR 74) suggests it is racing at its optimum level if the pace unfolds kindly.

runners_data.name: Magna
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Tony Carroll (5/42 in 14 days, a volume yard) who has won five of its last seven but all those wins came on soft or standard — good-to-firm is an unresolved question for a horse whose Flat record on that surface is 1/15; the tactical position is excellent (second-most natural front-running profile behind Moe's Legacy), but the going concern is legitimate and Molly Gunn's 5lb claim may not compensate for the surface worry.

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Carroll's second string and another hold-up type squeezed out of its natural position by the weight of closers in this field; its form on good and soft at 5f shows five places from 15 runs including two seconds at this trip on softer ground, yet Alexandra Egan (5lb claim) cannot manufacture clear runs that the closing style demands — the going is fine but the race shape is against it.

races.paceDynamic: Moe's Legacy is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f apprentice handicap on good-to-firm ground at Windsor, and with no serious challenger for the lead, Jack Nicholls can dictate a controlled, sustainable pace from the front without being pressured into burning early. The bulk of the field — Dark Alley, Kiss And Run, Alkuwarrior, London Is Blue, Beaumadier, Merrimack, Hint Of Humour, Too Darn Good and Angel Summer — all carry hold-up profiles, meaning the pack will be chasing a single front-runner around a flat, tight track, compressing the closing stages into a mass sprint finish. In The City and Magna offer the most natural prominent coverage behind Moe's Legacy, giving the leader a small buffer before the hold-up wave arrives. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the track map can place at the rear — Beaumadier, Merrimack, Hint Of Humour, Too Darn Good and Angel Summer cannot all find their natural backmarker position, and the most likely to genuinely secure it are Merrimack and Beaumadier given their 5f course-type experience, with the others forced into mid-division. This race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who can track the leader, avoid the traffic chaos deeper in the field, and pounce on a pace that is controlled rather than searingly fast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moe's Legacy Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Moe's Legacy settles cleanly in front and the hold-up runners fail to close the gap fast enough on this flat 5f track.
scenarios.body: Moe's Legacy sets a metronomic gallop from stall, controls every yard of the race, and the mass of closers behind face a compressed finishing straight with insufficient room to pick off a horse in front who has conserved energy; Windsor's flat 5f strongly suits those who can lead without being run at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Moe's Legacy fades in the final furlong after setting the pace and the closest trackers sweep past in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: In The City or Magna, sitting just off the leader's shoulder, benefit from a controlled pace that sees Moe's Legacy emptying near the line while the prominent pair have energy in reserve; on good-to-firm ground over 5f Windsor, horses who race within a length of the leader into the straight routinely overhaul a tired front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is quicker than expected and a genuine closer finds a clear run down the outside in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Merrimack or Beaumadier, the two hold-up types most likely to find their true backmarker position, produce a late run along the rail or wide outside the pack, but this shape requires both a faster pace and a clear passage — two conditions that are uncertain given the lone front-runner scenario; the compressed finish at Windsor over 5f makes this genuinely difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up contingent interferes mid-race, causing traffic issues that allow a free-moving horse to steal the race uncontested.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of five genuine closers into a crowded mid-division creates a realistic interference scenario where horses check, are hampered, or cannot find gaps, gifting any horse with a clear run an advantage even at modest ability; London Is Blue, with a strong winning record on good-to-firm ground, is best placed to capitalise if the pack behind disorganises itself.

watchPoints.text: Moe's Legacy (Jack Nicholls) — if this horse jumps cleanly and gets to the front without a challenge in the first furlong, it controls the entire race and all other tactical considerations become secondary; watch the first 2f for any rival testing the lead.

Magna (Molly Gunn) — the prominent style is perfectly placed to sit second behind Moe's Legacy, but if the going is riding faster than standard good-to-firm (Magna's win record is exclusively on slower surfaces), it may fail to sustain its effort in the final furlong despite ideal tactical position.

Merrimack and Beaumadier — the two most credible closers in the field, both redistributed into mid-division; if they cannot find clear running lanes between the 1f and 2f poles on Windsor's flat straight, any late challenge will be swallowed up by the horses already in prominent positions.

London Is Blue (Jack Callan, Robert Cowell 0/9 in 14 days) — the trainer's short-term form is poor but this horse has two wins on good and a recent second at 5f good; worth monitoring in-running to see whether Callan tracks the leader or gets trapped in the hold-up pack, as its chance is heavily position-dependent.

Trainer Warren Greatrex is 0/5 in the last 14 days and saddles both In The City and Dark Alley — if both runners underperform relative to their market positions, a yard-form issue rather than individual horse problems may be the explanation; note any early drifts in the market for either runner.

races.name: Follow @attheraces On X Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lucy The Wire
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with an OR of 120 and Oisin Murphy aboard, she has course-distance profile advantages and handles this going well (6/8 sim-going runs placed); STYLE_FIT tag means she is racing slightly out of her natural role but the solo lead opportunity effectively resolves that tension — the uncontested position suits her here.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply from 8f maiden form to 10f for Gemma Tutty's yard, which has found no winners in 13 attempts over 14 days; one placed run on similar going is her best comparable effort, and she will need the trip to unlock improvement to trouble Lucy The Wire.

runners_data.name: Star Suepreme
runners_data.note: 188-day absence is the dominant concern — she has just two career starts, both on Standard, and must now handle Good to Firm and a new trainer in Lemos De Souza; Lewis Edmunds takes the ride but a hold-up style over this trip on a first run back demands significant faith in her conditioning.

runners_data.name: Hotel California
runners_data.note: Entirely unexposed after two 8f runs on Standard for David Menuisier, so the step to 10f on fast turf is a double unknown; Saffie Osborne partners her and the ⚠ lightly-raced flag means her ultimate ceiling is genuinely unclear, which is both her risk and her theoretical appeal.

runners_data.name: Sweet Horizon
runners_data.note: Ran well enough at 10f Good last time (second) to suggest the trip and going combination suits; wears a hood (hg:b) and has had just 10 days since that run, so freshness is not a concern — her hold-up style means she needs a moderate pace collapse to get to Lucy The Wire, which this race shape is unlikely to produce.

races.paceDynamic: Lucy The Wire is the lone confirmed pace-setter in a five-runner field and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, she should dictate proceedings at a comfortable, uncontested gallop over this 1m2f Good to Firm Windsor trip. Ziata is the only other runner likely to race prominently, but with a style fit and form profile that suggests she will settle just behind rather than contest the front, meaning Lucy The Wire faces zero pressure from the front. Star Suepreme and Sweet Horizon are natural hold-up types who will track from midfield to rear, while Hotel California is an unknown quantity whose two starts were both at 8f on Standard ground. A solo leader controlling fractions on quick ground over a staying trip creates a race shape that strongly favours a horse able to travel prominently and sustain its effort — true late closers will need something to go wrong at the front to get involved, making the hold-up profile a secondary rather than primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Lucy The Wire dictates unchallenged at a fair but not punishing gallop and kicks clear from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Lucy The Wire, racing on going she handles and with Oisin Murphy in the plate, simply sets her own fractions and builds on her lead approaching the straight, leaving hold-up horses with too much ground to make up on fast going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just slow enough that hold-up horses conserve energy and have a decisive finishing kick in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sweet Horizon showed ability at 10f on Good and would be best placed of the hold-up brigade to pounce if Lucy The Wire has over-committed; Star Suepreme's long absence and unknown ceiling leave an outside possibility if returning well-schooled.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Ziata tracks the leader comfortably and proves stronger than Lucy The Wire inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Ziata has placed form at up to 10f and stepping up from a mile trip could unlock more stamina; if Lucy The Wire fades having led throughout, Ziata is ideally positioned to inherit the advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Improves To Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Hotel California, lightly raced and returning from 88 days off, produces an unseen level of ability on a surface and trip she has never encountered.
scenarios.body: David Menuisier's filly has scope for significant improvement given just two career starts, and Saffie Osborne's positive ride could see her travel into contention if the others disappoint; this scenario requires multiple coincidences and is a low-probability outlier.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Lucy The Wire is allowed to dictate an unusually slow early pace — if fractions are pedestrian, Sweet Horizon's finishing kick from the rear becomes a genuine winning threat rather than a minor one.

Hotel California's unknown ceiling after just two starts means Saffie Osborne could find a completely different horse at 10f on turf — monitor market moves close to post time as any significant support would be significant information.

Star Suepreme's 188-day layoff combined with a switch to fast ground and a new trainer is a combination of risk factors that makes her hard to assess — if she shows signs in the paddock of not being fully wound up, discount her entirely.

Ziata's yard (Gemma Tutty, 0/13 over 14 days) is in a cold spell; if the prominent position delivers her into contention it will be the horse rather than the training operation doing the heavy lifting.

races.name: British Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Harry Knows
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a solid form line of placed efforts on Good and Soft; Richard Hughes and Oisin Murphy is a strong combination, and tracking Angel Ang from gate to wire gives this horse the ideal tactical position in this shape.

runners_data.name: Q T Boy
runners_data.note: Finished last on debut at 6f on Good ground and carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag — David Evans sends out a hold-up type whose record gives no reason to expect a reversal here; 14 days since last run is not a concern but the form is.

runners_data.name: Rex Regum
runners_data.note: Two runs, both finishing 8th and 9th over 6f on Good; the fades-in-finish warning compounds what the bare form already shows, and the 7-pound claimer Molly Keegan-Price faces a tough ask in a race where position from the front matters most.

runners_data.name: Angel Ang
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who won impressively on debut at Sandown; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that she is listed as P here but should be L — in practice she is in the right role, and on Good to Firm ground with no pace rivals she has every chance to dictate at her leisure.

runners_data.name: Bollengo Boy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up type has two disappointing finishes over this course-and-distance combination on similar ground; a true closer by nature, the redistribution note means it will likely end up closer to the pace than suits, compounding the already modest form.

runners_data.name: Boysofwallstreet
runners_data.note: George Boughey's hold-up runner has been off 68 days — the longest layoff in the field — and a single run of 6th on Good is a thin profile; like Bollengo Boy, its natural rear-of-field position cannot be guaranteed given the number of closers, reducing its effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Down To You Kid
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's horse brings the most varied experience — three placed efforts including 2nds and 3rds over 6-7f on Good — and Pat Dobbs riding for Hannon's powerful operation is a positive; unlisted style (U) means tactical flexibility, and three placed runs suggest a competitive sort who could outrun its OR of 80.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Ang is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to match her stride for stride from the gates, she should establish a comfortable, uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground over Windsor's flat 6f. Harry Knows is the only other horse with a prominent profile and will likely track Angel Ang in second, meaning the tempo is set by one horse without serious challenge — a scenario that produces a steady-to-moderate gallop and gives the leader every chance to control the race from start to finish. Q T Boy, Rex Regum, Bollengo Boy, and Boysofwallstreet are all hold-up types, but the field contains more genuine closers than the race shape can accommodate comfortably: Bollengo Boy and Boysofwallstreet are true hold-up runners who have been mapped to midfield purely because all cannot sit at the rear, meaning at least some will end up closer to the pace than ideal. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — front-runners and trackers who can exploit the uncontested gallop set by Angel Ang — because the closers face a real risk of a moderate pace that does not generate enough of a finish to reel in those ahead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Angel Ang Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Ang leads uncontested and sets a comfortable gallop that suits her stamina reserves.
scenarios.body: Angel Ang dictates throughout on Good to Firm ground, with Harry Knows tracking in second and finding little pressure from behind; the pace never truly quickens sufficiently for the closers to run them down. Down To You Kid, proven over 6f on this going, is best placed of those behind to peg back the leaders if energy is conserved to the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Trackers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Ang sets a slightly faster-than-expected gallop and Harry Knows or Down To You Kid pick her off approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A moderate burn from the front becomes a strong enough clip to leave Angel Ang vulnerable inside the final furlong, and a prominent tracker with a clean position pounces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the hold-up horses get a proper end-to-end gallop to chase.
scenarios.body: Despite being shuffled closer than ideal due to redistribution, Boysofwallstreet or Bollengo Boy produce late runs if the pace genuinely heats up — though both face a style-fit discount given neither is truly in their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Gate-Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If form upsets strike and an exposed or unconsidered runner produces a big leap forward in performance.
scenarios.body: Q T Boy or Rex Regum, both of whom have underperformed their debut marks, produce an unexpected step forward in form that their previous figures give little reason to anticipate.

watchPoints.text: Angel Ang has no front-runner to race against — watch whether Ryan Kavanagh allows her to coast or asks her to pop the lid early, as either decision shapes the entire race.

Bollengo Boy and Boysofwallstreet cannot both find their natural hold-up berths — watch the early stride pattern to see which, if either, genuinely settles behind the field and which is forced wider or closer than ideal.

Down To You Kid with Pat Dobbs is the dark horse of the race — watch where Dobbs slots him in the first furlong, as a prominent early move could put this unexposed type in an unusually strong tactical position.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race by the going report, favouring horses with that going form; Harry Knows (3/4 on similar ground) and Down To You Kid (3/3) have the strongest sim-going profiles in the field.

races.name: Turbo Hoofing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: Rachel Cook & John Bridger's three-year-old has been running in races where he can push forward, but with Guernsey Angel locking down the lead here his natural prominent style is squeezed to midfield — a shape that blunts his chief weapon; his recent form string (256926) shows no wins at this level and his similar-going figures are modest.

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: T14 form of 2/7 for Christopher Mason gives some short-term confidence, and she showed a second and a third in recent runs, but this mare's true hold-up inclination is compromised by a field that is unlikely to generate the pace she needs, and she is pushed forward on the map only because the rear is already crowded.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter with Rossa Ryan aboard — David Evans sends him here off 23 days' rest and a T14 strike rate of 4/14, giving legitimate trainer confidence; his recent form reads poorly (645662) but controlling an uncontested lead on a flat track changes the equation entirely, and good-to-firm is fine for him.

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is the standout jockey booking in the race and Grace Harris has a T14 figure of 3/22, suggesting the stable is in reasonable nick; at 41 days off the track this hold-up specialist needs a searching pace to deliver his finish, and his similar-going record over this trip (0W0P from six) is a significant flag.

runners_data.name: Solar Invincible
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's three-year-old carries the tongue tie, has winning form on good ground over five furlongs, and Saffie Osborne takes off a useful 3lb; stepping up to 6f is the question mark given all five recent runs have been over five, but a prominent style on a flat track with a controlled pace ahead is an optimal setup if the extra furlong is within range.

runners_data.name: Exhibitioning
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's runner has finished tenth twice on good ground over 6f in his last two similar-going efforts, and a Finley Marsh claim cannot paper over a form string of 250-00 that signals a horse deeply out of form; the hood is listed but this is a hold-up type who needs a strong pace on a course that may not provide one.

races.paceDynamic: Guernsey Angel is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Rossa Ryan can dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on a flat 6f Windsor track that typically rewards those who can control from the front. Solar Invincible will track prominently just off the pace, giving Ryan a shadow to manage rather than a threat, while the hold-up horses Pull The Rug and Exhibitioning will need a strong enough tempo to manufacture their late momentum — something an unchallenged pace-setter is unlikely to provide. The field carries more prominent pace than the map can accommodate: Madman and Forever Glamorous are natural front-running or prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield because Guernsey Angel is likely to secure the rail and dictate, meaning those two are unlikely to race where they are most comfortable. This race shape firmly favours pace-pressing or prominent profiles able to track the controlled leader — a steady gallop on good-to-firm ground will compress the finishing kick for true hold-up horses and leave them with too little to pick up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Guernsey Angel Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Guernsey Angel secures the lead unchallenged and sets a comfortable, even gallop that fails to produce a strong finishing surge.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan dictates every yard on the flat Windsor circuit, building a rhythm that punishes horses needing a true pace to close into; prominent types who track the leader have first use of the real estate turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Solar Invincible or a redistributed prominent type tracks Guernsey Angel closely enough to strike immediately once the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: A race run at a moderate pace over 6f on good-to-firm ground can still produce a clean strike from a horse sitting second or third if the leader flattens inside the final furlong; Solar Invincible's five-furlong course form and prominent style set up perfectly for this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the hold-up horses get a genuine end-to-end gallop to close into.
scenarios.body: Pull The Rug with Oisin Murphy has the class and tactical engine to benefit if a real pace develops, though his recent going stats show little encouragement; Exhibitioning would also need a strong tempo but has finished tenth on this ground twice, making it an unlikely beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clean Shape
scenarios.trigger: If there is a stumble, wide draw traffic, or early incident that scrambles the anticipated pace order completely.
scenarios.body: Madman, displaced from his natural prominent role, might find a gap if the field bunches and reshuffles through the early stages; Forever Glamorous could also benefit from disorganisation if she finds clear daylight sooner than expected.

watchPoints.text: Guernsey Angel is the only confirmed pace-setter — watch whether Rossa Ryan is allowed to drift into a very slow early gallop, which would collapse the race into a sprint finish that could wrong-foot the hold-up brigade completely.

Solar Invincible's step up from five furlongs to six furlongs is unproven — watch the first two furlongs to see whether Saffie Osborne settles her smoothly behind Guernsey Angel or whether she over-races, burning energy she will need at the finish.

Madman and Forever Glamorous are both likely to find themselves racing out of their preferred position — watch whether either horse becomes restless or pulls early, as that wasted energy would damage their already-compressed chances in a pace-controlled race.

Pull The Rug's 41-day absence and Oisin Murphy's positional instincts are worth watching in the first furlong — if Murphy attempts to manufacture a forward position rather than accepting rear ground, the shape of the race could shift slightly and create a more compressed mid-race pace.

races.name: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap Stakes (Windsor Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on Good recently and has strong course form; steps up to 6f here where he has also won, making the trip no concern, and William Carson's positive forcing style suits tracking Dandana closely from a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Mesaafi
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose best form comes at 5f on Good, and despite being mapped to midfield the redistribution note reflects that true closers are stacked in this field; the step to 6f and the need to make ground from a rear position on a flat track are concerns.

runners_data.name: Maelstrom
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent racer returning from 252 days off who has wins at this trip on Good, but the long absence is a significant flag and the crowded prominent positions mean he is unlikely to secure his preferred racing spot — his chance depends heavily on fitness from that lengthy break.

runners_data.name: Regional Rock
runners_data.note: Strong recent profile for a 3yo, having finished second twice before winning last time out all at 6f, with a useful Rossa Ryan booking; races prominently and the sim-going record of 2/3 runners placed makes him one of the best-qualified in the field for this surface.

runners_data.name: Amazonian Dream
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 6f recently and is in consistent form, but Oisin Murphy faces a challenge here as this horse's natural front-running tendency cannot be accommodated cleanly with Dandana dominant, meaning she will likely have to race further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Hucklesbrook
runners_data.note: An 80-day absence is the primary flag, carrying top weight of 138lbs and a hold-up style; his last two runs were mid-field finishes on Good ground at this trip and he will need everything to click from an unfavoured deep position.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 6f on Good and is consistent from a prominent position; Finley Marsh rides and the horse's profile of tracking the pace and grinding suits a scenario where the gallop is honest rather than false.

runners_data.name: Uncle Don
runners_data.note: Returned a non-winner in 15 runs but has placed at this trip on Good; races prominently but the recent record suggests he finds it hard to win from that position without an exceptionally weak race developing around him.

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good ground and holds some hold-up form credentials; Pat Dobbs takes over for William Haggas whose runners have a reasonable 5/28 in 14 days, though the horse's sim-going record of 11/15 suggests he handles this surface less reliably than his headline form implies.

runners_data.name: Nad Alshiba Green
runners_data.note: Placed at 5f and 6f on Good from a prominent style and returns from 63 days off; the trainer Clive Cox has 4/21 in 14 days which is respectable, and this horse has the class and course-relevant profile to be competitive if fit.

runners_data.name: Willem Twee
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer who has been consistent over 7f on Standard surfaces but all five recent runs are on All-Weather, making the switch to Good turf at 6f a significant unknown; the sim-going record of 1/15 is a serious concern.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Headgear-wearing hold-up type with a modest recent record, finishing 10th, 6th, 12th, 6th and 5th in his last five; at OR=85 and with this pattern of running it is hard to construct a convincing winning scenario even in the most favourable shape.

runners_data.name: Dandana
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Simon & Ed Crisford with David Egan, has the highest OR in the field at 90 and won at 6f on Good; the style-fit tag reflects that the controlled leader role here is slightly out of natural character but she is the clearest pace influence and controls how this race is framed.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield accurately reflects the crowded rear positions in this field; has one win at 6f on Standard and a recent run of 6th on Good — the move to Good turf and the inability to get a clear run from back are twin obstacles.

races.paceDynamic: Dandana is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to match her early, she should secure a clean, uncontested lead and control tempo on Good to Firm ground at Windsor. Regional Rock, Ancient State, Sudden Flight, and Uncle Don will press for prominent positions just off the pace, creating a competitive early exchanges behind Dandana but leaving her relatively undisturbed in front. The field carries considerably more pace than the map can accommodate — Maelstrom, Amazonian Dream, and Star Chorus are genuine prominent or hold-up types who will struggle to secure their natural position and are likely to be shuffled wider or further back than ideal. A controlled, honest pace set by a single leader on fast ground over 6f at Windsor historically favours prominent racers tracking close to the pace rather than deep hold-up horses, and that is the profile this race shape rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandana Leads, Pressers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Dandana controls from the front and sets a measured but honest gallop, allowing the closest prominent chasers to track her at optimum striking range.
scenarios.body: Dandana sets a sustainable tempo and the race becomes a test of quality in the final 2f, with those who have tracked closest through the race having enough fuel to sustain their challenge; the Good to Firm surface suits horses with a fluid, prominent style who have been switching off rather than burning energy chasing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Dandana encounters minimal pressure and slows the pace to a crawl, setting it up for a sprint finish that rewards those in front.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race punishes deep hold-up horses who cannot quicken from far back over 6f, and Dandana's OR=90 and front-running ability becomes a significant weapon if she can coast through the middle stages and sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hot, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners behind Dandana push hard early and the pace becomes genuinely strong, burning off front-end horses late.
scenarios.body: An honest or above-average pace over 6f on fast ground opens the door for hold-up types to find their running late as the leaders tire; however, several of the best-positioned hold-up horses in this field are redistributed from their natural roles, which limits the reliability of this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic Issues Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the large 14-runner field produces significant traffic problems through the early stages, scrambling normal running positions.
scenarios.body: With so many horses compressed into a flat 6f track and multiple genuine pace types forced out of position, a runner who finds a clear run from an unexpected angle could benefit disproportionately; this scenario is low probability but non-trivial given the field size.

watchPoints.text: Dandana's early sectionals are critical — if she bowls along uncontested and sets only a moderate pace, the horses closest to her (Regional Rock, Ancient State) inherit a decisive positional advantage that the hold-up brigade cannot overcome from further back.

Maelstrom returns from 252 days off and, while talented at this trip, could show signs of rustiness or overcook the early pace having been deprived of racing; monitor how sharply he breaks and whether he burns himself out in the first furlong fighting for a position he may not get.

The 14-runner field in a flat 6f sprint means early traffic and positional scrambling are likely; horses with wide draws or who fail to break cleanly — particularly redistributed hold-up types like Mesaafi and Star Chorus — could find themselves in a worse position than their paper style already implies.

Another Abbot and Hucklesbrook are the two hold-up runners with the clearest winning form at this trip, but both carry concerns (17-day turnaround and top weight for Hucklesbrook; sim-going record for Another Abbot) that reduce confidence even if the pace genuinely collapses late.

Amazonian Dream with Oisin Murphy is a runner who looks considerably more potent on paper if she can replicate her recent 6f Good win, but her inability to get a natural prominent position here means Murphy will face a tactical puzzle from a disadvantaged starting point in the race shape.

races.name: Debbie And Kieron Silver Wedding Celebration Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who finds this Good to Firm Windsor mile within her comfort zone; two placed efforts at this trip on Standard give her solid form lines, though Finley Marsh needs to navigate a field crowded with similar types to find clear running in the straight.

runners_data.name: Star Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical agenda for this entire race; Oisin Murphy is booked, which is a significant booking upgrade, but the STYLE_FIT flag is relevant — she is stepping slightly out of role for Denis Coakley and her recent form over 10f on Good ground suggests stamina rather than pace is her strength.

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old has form figures of 6-2-7-7-7 in recent starts but that second at 8f on Soft is a legitimate course-and-distance pointer; Jack Callan claims 3lb and his last 24-day freshen-up could suit a horse who needs time between runs.

runners_data.name: Cixi
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has no wins or placed efforts in similar going in her last six outings, which is a concern on Good to Firm; Pat Dobbs takes the ride but the hold-up style and lack of a placed effort on fast ground makes her hard to enthuse about tactically.

runners_data.name: Box Clever
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing headgear (p — probably a hood) for Jonathan Portman, with a win and three places from eight runs on Good ground — the style profile fits this race shape beautifully as she can track Star Of Dubai from the ideal second position; Rob Hornby is a polished judge of pace.

runners_data.name: Khuskhas
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's three-year-old won over this trip on Good ground as recently as four starts ago, which is the key form line; David Egan takes over and the blinkers are noted — however, this horse's natural hold-up style means she is one of several closers competing for rear-ground that simply may not materialise today.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) for Ed Dunlop, who has fired one winner from twelve runners in the last 14 days — the 38-day break is the longest in this field and she must be treated with some caution on form recency; two runs on Good ground yielded finishes of 6th and 5th, suggesting the surface is not a concern but she hasn't shown enough to feature prominently.

runners_data.name: Berlinetta
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's three-year-old has run five times on Good or Good to Firm ground for four placed or mid-table finishes — her best efforts have come at shorter trips (5-6f) and stepping up to a mile on this surface is not obviously in her favour; a true hold-up type who has been placed to midfield on the map, she will need more pace in the race than Star Of Dubai is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Denby's Dream
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's three-year-old has a win over this exact course and distance on Good ground, which is the standout form angle; Rossa Ryan takes over and the hood (h) is noted — she is a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the crowded closer profile of this field, so she needs Star Of Dubai to press a stronger pace than anticipated.

races.paceDynamic: Star Of Dubai is the lone confirmed front-runner here, and with Oisin Murphy in the saddle she is likely to be deployed prominently from the outset, setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo over Windsor's flat mile. The going is Good to Firm, which rewards horses travelling smoothly rather than those who need a true slog, and a controlled pace from Star Of Dubai will likely compress the field through the middle stages, leaving little gap for hold-up horses to exploit late. Box Clever is the only other genuinely prominent type and will track Star Of Dubai, meaning the shape is effectively a single pace-setter with one close shadow — a classic scenario that suits horses who can race in second or third and pounce from a position of cover. This race shape favours prominent-to-midfield types who can travel within the pace rather than true closers who need a strong gallop to close into; three of the hold-up horses — Khuskhas, Berlinetta, and Denby's Dream — are genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with closers and they are unlikely to secure their natural position cleanly, meaning the hold-up dynamic is further diluted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Box Clever Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Dubai sets a measured, uncontested pace and Box Clever tracks her comfortably before producing a clean turn of foot entering the home straight.
scenarios.body: Star Of Dubai's lone lead gifts Box Clever an ideal stalking position, and on Good to Firm ground a horse who can press the pace from second or third without burning petrol has a decisive structural advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Burst Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that the field bunches and a sharp late sprint opens the door for a hold-up type finishing from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the middle mile can compress groups and occasionally allow a horse with a sharp sprint to cut through — Eazy On The Eye or Toralou, tracking from midfield, could benefit if the field fans wide in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Dubai is allowed to roll along at a genuine clip and simply outstays rivals who can never get close enough to challenge.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground over a flat mile, a front-runner who controls fractions entirely on her own terms can prove very difficult to reel in — Star Of Dubai's form includes placed efforts at this trip and her prominent style is well-suited to Windsor's configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and one of the hold-up types — forced wider and later than ideal — produces an unexpected late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a faster-than-expected tempo from Star Of Dubai and Box Clever to create genuine late ground, which is unlikely given the lone pace-setter dynamic; Khuskhas has form on Good ground and Denby's Dream has winning course-and-distance form, but both are racing out of their natural position making this low-probability.

watchPoints.text: Star Of Dubai's uncontested lead is the structural pivot of this race — if Murphy elects to dawdle through the middle stages, the entire field compresses and her chance of winning on the bridle increases dramatically while hold-up types lose their weapon.

Box Clever's prominent style and Good-ground form make her the natural beneficiary of this race shape, but her last run was 28 days ago and she wore headgear last time — watch for whether the hood is retained and how quickly she travels to the front group.

Denby's Dream's winning course-and-distance form on Good is the most directly relevant piece of evidence in the race, but she will be shuffled further back than ideal in a field of hold-up types — watch if Ryan attempts to be more positive early given the race shape.

Three runners — Khuskhas, Berlinetta, and Denby's Dream — are all genuine hold-up types forced to compete for ground that a slow pace will deny them; if they all sit in behind a moderate gallop, they effectively cancel each other out and the prominent types dominate.

Going is officially Good to Firm at the 8:00 race based on the going report, faster than the declared Good — horses with strong Standard/All-Weather form (Eazy On The Eye, Toralou) may find the quicker surface marginally less suitable than their form suggests.

races.name: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: The clear pace angle in this race — uncontested lead on good-to-firm suits, Windsor 1m2f should see it travel comfortably, Rob Hornby rode it to its last two wins, and six days since last run looks fine; STYLE_FIT flag is a minor concern only if something pushes it harder than expected early.

runners_data.name: Katalyst
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's 3yo has produced modest form at best (best effort a 2nd at 9f on Good), carries the highest weight for a hold-up horse with little pace shape benefit, and the step up to 1m2f has not been convincingly flagged by his 8f-dominated form history.

runners_data.name: Sweep In Time
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's hold-up performer has a single run over 10f which yielded a 4th on Good — a clear distance positive — but as a genuine rear-of-field type now mapped into midfield, David Egan will struggle to find the natural rhythm that brings out its best; 18 days off is manageable.

runners_data.name: Thomas Picton
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's runner has been consistently beaten in midfield on Good ground over shorter (four runs, never better than 7th), longest layoff in the field at 65 days, and as an authentic hold-up horse pushed forward on the map, Rose Dawes faces a difficult tactical puzzle with an apprentice's 5lb claim offering little compensatory upside.

runners_data.name: Give Me Sun
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 10f on Good ground — the trip is its best friend here — and Benoit de la Sayette is a high-quality booking for a 54-rated horse; as a true hold-up type shuffled into the midfield projection, it will need a faster pace than Takeitorleaveit is likely to set, but its stamina credentials are the best of the hold-up group.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 3yo is the most interesting hold-up challenger — won over 8f on Good, placed at 8f on Soft, and Rossa Ryan is a smart jockey booking; the ⚠ fade flag is a concern in a slowly-run race that does not suit rearward types, but its recent form (1,2) is the best in the field behind the pacesetter.

runners_data.name: Rugby Union
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence is the most notable jockey angle in the field, but the ⚠ fade flag combined with four consecutive placed or beaten efforts over 10f on Good, and its redistribution from a natural hold-up berth, means the tactical ask is significant even for Murphy; trainer Gemma Tutty has not fired a winner in 13 recent starts.

runners_data.name: Time To Sparkle
runners_data.note: James Keane's runner has placed twice over 10f on Good ground — genuinely competitive at this trip — and Jack Mitchell is a polished jockey, but 59 days off is a query, and as a horse whose natural station is at the rear, finding a prominent enough position to exploit a slow pace will require it to race against instinct throughout.

races.paceDynamic: Takeitorleaveit is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Windsor handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop over the good-to-firm turf without any pressure applied in the early stages. The Windsor figure-of-eight layout over this trip asks horses to travel efficiently and hold their position rather than make ground from deep, meaning a steady, uncontested pace is the most likely race shape from the outset. With Takeitorleaveit dictating alone, the race will lack the searching tempo that typically brings hold-up horses into play late, favouring runners who can sit close to the pace and produce a measured, grinding finish from the front or prominent positions. This race shape clearly favours the prominent/front-running profile — Takeitorleaveit is best placed to exploit its uncontested lead, while hold-up horses will be fighting an unfavourable tactical battle. Note that the field contains significantly more genuine hold-up types than can all race from their natural position — Sweep In Time, Thomas Picton, Give Me Sun, Rugby Union, and Time To Sparkle are all authentic rear-of-field horses redistributed into the midfield on the pace map, with only those quickest to adapt or best suited in other ways likely to pose a real threat to the pacesetter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Takeitorleaveit Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit breaks cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead at a controlled tempo, producing a true test of stamina over staying ground.
scenarios.body: Takeitorleaveit settles in front at its own pace, the field strings out behind on the good-to-firm turf, and those with sustained galloping ability rather than a sharp turn of foot hold the advantage as the race unfolds steadily into the straight. The horse's recent consistent form, prominent style, and a jockey in Rob Hornby who can judge the pace from the front make this the dominant scenario in a race that has no early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the controlled lead still takes its toll in the closing stages, allowing the best-staying hold-up horses to pick up in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Even at a steady tempo, the 1m2f trip on good-to-firm turf over Windsor's unique track can expose horses who have been working harder than they look mid-race, enabling any runner with genuine stamina reserves to close late. My Old Mate's recent winning form and Time To Sparkle's placed efforts over 10f on Good ground make them the most credible beneficiaries of this shape, though both face the structural challenge of being held up in a race that does not encourage late rushes.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If a second horse — most likely one of the nominally midfield-placed but naturally prominent types — pushes up to challenge Takeitorleaveit in the middle stages, creating a genuine duel.
scenarios.body: Should the pace lift mid-race through a rival pressing forward, the race becomes a two-horse duel from some way out, and the horse with the superior stamina and handicap mark wins a tighter finish. Rugby Union or Time To Sparkle are the most likely to adopt a more prominent position than their style tag suggests, but both carry the caution of fading in finish or redistribution from their natural hold-up role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit is caught wide, pressed unexpectedly, or fades in the final furlong, leaving a chaotic finish that a fresh horse or big-priced runner exploits.
scenarios.body: With Katalyst, Sweep In Time, and Thomas Picton all showing limited recent positivity in the form book and racing out of their natural positions, this scenario depends on multiple things going wrong at once and is a genuinely low-probability outcome. Give Me Sun, placed twice over 10f on Good ground, is the most likely beneficiary of a chaotic or messy finish from this otherwise unfancied group.

watchPoints.text: Takeitorleaveit is the only confirmed front-runner in an 8-runner field — watch whether Rob Hornby elects to go hard early or settle for a crawl, as the entire race shape hinges on the pace it chooses to set.

My Old Mate carries a ⚠ fade flag and is ridden by Rossa Ryan from a hold-up position — if the pace is genuinely slow, Ryan may be forced to make his move earlier than ideal, which could expose the stamina weakness flagged in its profile.

Oisin Murphy on Rugby Union is worth monitoring in the early stages — Murphy is capable of positioning a natural hold-up horse prominently if he reads the lack of pace early, which could trigger SCENARIO_C and turn this into a two-horse race mid-race.

Five horses in this field (Sweep In Time, Thomas Picton, Give Me Sun, Rugby Union, Time To Sparkle) are genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield on the map — watch how congested the middle sections become and whether any of them can find clear daylight to make a meaningful late challenge.

The going is reported as Good To Firm for this 1m2f race despite the card header showing Good — on good-to-firm Windsor turf, a sustained gallop can bring stamina into sharper focus, and Give Me Sun's and Time To Sparkle's placed form over 10f on Good makes them worth monitoring if the tempo quickens at all.
